title: Use the training segment marker to identify the end of the RMS section during Day 1 training
summary: Use the Day 1 training video’s explicit RMS-section-end marker (the on-screen reference “Aveva Walkthrough 32” and the spoken cue “I think that ends the RMS section”) to recognize when the training transitions away from the RMS portion, including the break/pacing discussion.
when_to_use: When you are following UPSFORTNA OptiSweep Training Day 1 and need a grounded cue that the session is transitioning away from the RMS portion so you can prepare for the next topic (including break/pacing).
not_for: Do not use this as an operational troubleshooting procedure for RMS, WCS/Helix DB, or any live system behavior. This segment is a training-session transition marker only.

roles_and_responsibilities.responsibility: Use the video’s RMS-section-end marker (on-screen “Aveva Walkthrough 32” and spoken cue) to determine when the RMS portion ends and the session transitions to the next topic.

access_or_tools_needed: UPSFORTNA OptiSweep Training Day 1 video player
Ability to view the training video frame containing the text "Aveva Walkthrough 32"

visual_references.description: Training video frame showing the on-screen reference text "Aveva Walkthrough 32" and the RMS-section-end spoken cue context.

steps.title: Locate the training video frame that shows the slide reference text "Aveva Walkthrough 32"
steps.purpose: Provide a visual anchor for the exact segment where the RMS section ends.
steps.instruction: In the UPSFORTNA OptiSweep Training Day 1 video, navigate to the frame captured in segment training_video_day1_segment_0051 and confirm the on-screen text reads "Aveva Walkthrough 32".
steps.expected_result: You can see the training frame with the OCR text "Aveva Walkthrough 32" at the RMS-section-end transition segment.
steps.healthy_condition: The frame clearly shows the text "Aveva Walkthrough 32" (with the surrounding training frame context).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot find a frame where the on-screen text reads "Aveva Walkthrough 32".

actions.label: Verify slide reference frame
actions.exact_action: Locate the training video frame containing the text "Aveva Walkthrough 32".

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot find the "Aveva Walkthrough 32" frame, stop and ask the trainer for the correct timestamp/segment.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Artifact OCR shows "Aveva Walkthrough 32" and nearby transcript includes the RMS-end cue.
A visible training frame shows the text "Aveva Walkthrough 32".

steps.title: Listen for the spoken cue indicating the RMS section is ending
steps.purpose: Confirm the transition away from the RMS portion using the explicit spoken marker.
steps.instruction: Listen in the same segment for the spoken phrase indicating the RMS section is ending (example cue: "I think that ends the RMS section").
steps.expected_result: You hear the spoken cue that the RMS section is ending ("I think that ends the RMS section").
steps.healthy_condition: The spoken cue occurs during the segment where the RMS-end marker is presented.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot identify the spoken RMS-end cue in the segment.

actions.label: Confirm spoken RMS-end cue
actions.exact_action: Listen for the spoken cue indicating the RMS section is ending (e.g., transcript phrase "I think that ends the RMS section").

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot find the RMS-end spoken cue, stop and ask the trainer for the correct timestamp/segment.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Transcript includes: "I think that ends the RMS section".
The transcript explicitly states that the RMS section is ending during this training segment.

steps.title: Follow the spoken transition discussion (break/pacing) to align with the training pace
steps.purpose: Use the transition discussion to prepare for the next topic and manage pacing (break vs. being behind schedule).
steps.instruction: During the transition segment after the RMS-end cue, follow the discussion about taking a break and schedule status (e.g., whether to take a break and that the team is behind schedule).
steps.expected_result: You recognize that the session is transitioning and that the speakers discuss break/pacing (including being behind schedule).
steps.healthy_condition: The transition discussion includes a break prompt and schedule/pacing remarks (e.g., "Do you wanna give a break?" and "We're behind, so we need to get go").
steps.failure_condition: The transition discussion is not recognized or does not match the expected break/pacing context for this segment.

actions.label: Confirm break/pacing discussion
actions.exact_action: Follow the spoken transition discussion (e.g., whether to take a break) to align with the training pace described in the segment.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the segment does not contain the expected break/pacing discussion, stop and ask the trainer for the correct timestamp/segment.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Transcript includes: "Do you wanna give a break?" and "We're behind, so we need to get go."
The speakers discuss whether to take a break, indicating this segment is a training-session transition rather than an operational instruction segment.

success_criteria: You identify the RMS-section-end transition using both the on-screen reference "Aveva Walkthrough 32" and the spoken cue "I think that ends the RMS section".
You recognize the session transition and the break/pacing discussion (including being behind schedule) so you can prepare for the next topic.
healthy_conditions: The video frame with OCR text "Aveva Walkthrough 32" is present in the RMS-end transition segment.
The spoken cue "I think that ends the RMS section" is audible in that segment.
A break/pacing discussion occurs immediately after the RMS-end cue.
failure_conditions: The "Aveva Walkthrough 32" frame cannot be located.
The spoken RMS-end cue cannot be found.
The break/pacing discussion is missing or does not match the expected transition context.
escalation_guidance: If you cannot find the RMS-end spoken cue or the "Aveva Walkthrough 32" frame, stop and ask the trainer for the correct timestamp/segment.
